Timber Sycamore was a classified weapons supply and training program run by the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ ___E:Central Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ (CIA) and supported by the ___E:United Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom)___ and some ___E:Arab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs)___ intelligence services, including ___E:Saudi intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Intelligence_Presidency)___ .
The aim of the program was to remove Syrian president ___E:Bashar al-Assad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashar_al-Assad)___ from power.

Launched in 2012 or 2013, it supplied money, weaponry and training to ___E:Syrian opposition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_opposition)___ groups fighting Syrian government forces in the ___E:Syrian Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_civil_war)___ .

Many of these weapons ultimately ended up in the hands of extremist groups, including ___E:al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ , contributing to the rise and empowerment of ___E:ISIS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISIS)___ in 2014.
According to US officials, the program was run by the CIA's ___E:Special Activities Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Activities_Division)___  and has trained thousands of rebels.
U.S.

President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ secretly authorized the CIA to begin arming Syria's embattled rebels in 2013. The program became public knowledge in mid-2016.
One consequence of the program has been a flood of US weapons including assault rifles, mortars and rocket-propelled grenades into the Middle East's black market.

Critics of the program within the Obama administration viewed it as ineffective and expensive, and raised concerns about seizure of weaponry by ___E:Islamist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamism)___ groups and about Timber Sycamore-backed rebels fighting alongside the ___E:Al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ -affiliated ___E:Al-Nusra Front U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Nusra_Front)___ and its allies.

In July 2017, US officials stated that Timber Sycamore would be phased out, with funds possibly redirected to fighting the ___E:Islamic State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State)___ (IS), or to offering rebel forces defensive capabilities.

CIA director ___E:David Petraeus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Petraeus)___ first proposed a covert program of arming and training rebels in the summer of 2012. Initially ___E:President Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ rejected the proposal, but later agreed, partially due to lobbying by foreign leaders, including from ___E:King Abdullah II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullah_II_of_Jordan)___ of Jordan and Israeli Prime Minister ___E:Benjamin Netanyahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu)___ .

Timber Sycamore began in late 2012   or early 2013, and was similar to other Pentagon or CIA-run weapons routing and training programs that were established in previous decades to support foreign rebel forces.

Greg Miller and Adam Entous of The Washington Post stated that "The operation has served as the centerpiece of the U.S. strategy to press Syrian President ___E:Bashar al-Assad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashar_al-Assad)___ to step aside."  The program's principal backers were the United States and Saudi Arabia, but it was also supported by some other regional Arab governments, and by the United Kingdom.
While Saudi Arabia provides more money and weaponry, the United States leads training in military equipment.
The program was based in Jordan, due to that country's proximity to the battlefields in Syria.
According to The New York Times , the program initially allowed US forces to train Syrian rebels in use of military equipment, but not to directly provide the equipment itself.
A few months after its creation, it was amended to allow the CIA to both train and equip rebel forces.
Saudi Arabia has provided military equipment, and covert financing of rebel forces has also been provided by Qatar, Turkey and Jordan.
Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey shipped thousands of rifles, hundreds of machine guns, and large amounts of ammunition to Syrian rebels in 2012 before the program's launch.

The CIA helped arrange some of the arms purchases for the Saudis, including a large deal in Croatia in 2012.  A classified ___E:US State Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_State_Department)___ cable signed by ___E:Secretary of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State)___ ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ reported that Saudi donors were a major support for ___E:Sunni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni)___ militant forces globally, and some American officials worried that rebels being supported had ties to ___E:Al Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Qaeda)___ .

The existence of Timber Sycamore was revealed by The New York Times and Al Jazeera in June 2016, after Jane's Defence Weekly reported, in late 2015, that the US Federal Business Opportunities website was soliciting contracts to ship thousands of tons of weapons from Eastern Europe to ___E:Taşucu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ta%C5%9Fucu)___ , Turkey and ___E:Aqaba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aqaba)___ , Jordan.

Timber Sycamore was run by the Military Operations Command (MOC) in Amman  and provided ___E:Kalashnikov assault rifles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalashnikov_rifle)___ , ___E:mortars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortar_(weapon))___ , ___E:rocket-propelled grenades U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket-propelled_grenade)___ , ___E:TOW U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BGM-71_TOW)___ ___E:anti-tank guided missiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-tank_guided_missile)___ , ___E:night vision goggles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_vision_goggles)___ , pickup trucks, and other weapons to prospective Syrian rebel forces.
Many of the weapons were purchased in the Balkans or other locations in Eastern Europe, and then routed to Syrian rebel forces and training camps by Jordanian security services.
CIA paramilitary operatives trained Syrian rebels in use of the weaponry.

According to Charles Lister at The Daily Beast there were at least 50 vetted rebel groups fighting in Syria that received weapons or training through the program after late 2012;  the exact number is not known.
According to American officials, the program was highly effective, training and equipping thousands of US-backed fighters to make substantial battlefield gains.

American officials stated that the program began to lose effectiveness after ___E:Russia intervened militarily U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_military_intervention_in_the_Syrian_Civil_War)___ in the ___E:Syrian Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Civil_War)___ .  ___E:David Ignatius U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ignatius)___ , writing in The Washington Post , remarked that while the CIA program ultimately failed in its objective of removing Assad from power, it was hardly "bootless": "The program pumped many hundreds of millions of dollars to many dozens of militia groups.
One knowledgeable official estimates that the CIA-backed fighters may have killed or wounded 100,000 Syrian soldiers and their allies over the past four years."

Timber Sycamore is distinct from the ___E:Syrian Train and Equip Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Train_and_Equip_Program)___ , another Pentagon program established to train Syrian rebel forces to fight against the ___E:Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant)___ (ISIL)   The Pentagon made it clear their goal in Syria and Iraq was 'to fight ISIS and fight ISIS only [and] we've asked [our partner forces] to be committed to that same mission' and that they would not fight Assad's military.

US-backed rebels often fought alongside ___E:al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ 's ___E:al-Nusra Front U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Nusra_Front)___ against Ba'athist forces, and some of the US-supplied weapons were seized by the al-Nusra Front.

This had been a major concern within the Obama administration when the program was first proposed in 2012. There were also allegations of U.S.-backed militias carrying out ___E:summary killings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summary_killing)___ of detainees.

Following the ___E:Russian military intervention in Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_intervention_in_Syria)___ , pro-American militias began losing ground in late 2016, after a year of intensive aerial bombing campaigns of the ___E:Russian Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Air_Force)___ .

The program remains classified,    and many details about the program remain unknown, including the total amount of support, the range of weapons transferred, the depth of training provided, the types of US trainers involved, and the exact rebel groups being supported.
However, an opinion piece in The Canberra Times said that two thousand tons of Eastern European-manufactured weapons had been delivered to Aqaba by April 2016.
The US delivered weapons via ___E:Ramstein Air Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramstein_Air_Base)___ in Germany – possibly in breach of German laws.

According to American and Jordanian officials, weapons shipped into Jordan by the CIA and Saudi Arabia were stolen by Jordanian intelligence officials in the ___E:General Intelligence Directorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Intelligence_Directorate_(Jordan))___ and sold on the black market.

The magnitude of the theft amounted to millions of dollars, and ___E:FBI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation)___ officials state that some of the stolen weapons were later used to kill two American contractors, two Jordanians and one South African at a police training station in Jordan in the ___E:2015 Amman shooting attack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Amman_shooting_attack)___ .
Arms received via Timber Sycamore have flooded Middle Eastern black markets with heavy weaponry.
Jordanian officials state that Jordanian intelligence officers who stole the program's weapons used the profits to purchase luxury items, with knowledge of superior officers.
The thefts were halted after months of complaints by the American and Saudi governments, the program's main backers.

According to Jordanian officials, several intelligence officers were fired, but their profits were not confiscated. (In Jordan, the General Intelligence Directorate is second only to the monarchy in power and prestige.)  Jordan's minister for state and media affairs Mohammad Al-Momani stated that the allegations were incorrect.
Prior to the Syrian Civil War, southern Syria and northern Jordan were a conduit for other smuggling operations.

The advent of the war transformed the region into a center for smuggling weapons, and the more formal support provided by Timber Sycamore only intensified the scale of smuggling operations on the border.

Major smuggling centers include ___E:bazaars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bazaar)___ established at ___E:Ma'an U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma%27an)___ in southern Jordan, ___E:Sahab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahab_district)___ in Amman, and in the ___E:Jordan River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_River)___ Valley.

An investigation by journalists Phil Sands and Suha Maayeh revealed that rebels supplied with weapons from the Amman MOC sold a portion of them to local arms dealers, often to raise cash to pay additional fighters.

Some MOC-supplied weapons were sold to ___E:Bedouin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedouin)___ traders referred to locally as "The Birds" in ___E:Lajat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lajat)___ , a volcanic plateau northeast of ___E:Daraa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daraa)___ , Syria.

According to rebel forces, the Bedouins would then trade the weapons to the ___E:Islamic State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State)___ (IS) group, who would place orders using the encrypted ___E:WhatsApp U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WhatsApp)___ messaging service.
Two rebel commanders and a ___E:United Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom)___ weapons monitoring organization maintain that MOC–supplied weapons have made their way to IS forces.

A 2017 study conducted by ___E:Conflict Armament Research U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conflict_Armament_Research)___ at the behest of the ___E:European Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union)___ and ___E:Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Gesellschaft_f%C3%BCr_Internationale_Zusammenarbeit)___ does not mention Timber Sycamore but found that external support for anti-Assad Syrian rebels "significantly augmented the quantity and quality of weapons available to [ISIL] forces,"  including, in the most rapid case diversion they documented,  "anti-tank weapons purchased by the United States that ended up in possession of the Islamic State within two months of leaving the factory."  The study traced the provenance of some weapons in detail but found no instance in which US arms supplied to the ___E:YPG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YPG)___ –led ___E:Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Democratic_Forces)___ to fight IS ended up in the arsenal of IS.

In July 2017, anonymous officials stated that President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ , in consultation with National Security Adviser ___E:H. R. McMaster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._R._McMaster)___ and CIA Director ___E:Mike Pompeo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo)___ , had decided to phase out support for anti-Assad Syrian rebel forces, possibly redirecting resources to fighting ISIL, to offering rebel forces defensive capabilities, or to other operations in the region.

The officials said that the decision was made prior to Trump's participation in the ___E:G-20 summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_G20_Hamburg_summit)___ and 7 July meeting with Russian president ___E:Vladimir Putin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin)___ .

Several officials characterized the decision as a "major concession" to Russia, with one remarking: "Putin won in Syria."  However, another official stated that ending the program was not a major concession due to Assad's recent victories in the Syrian Civil War, but rather "a signal to Putin that the administration wants to improve ties to Russia."  Some members of the Obama administration reportedly had wished to scrap the program because some rebels armed and trained by the program had joined ISIL and related groups.

A ___E:related US military program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Train_and_Equip_Program)___ to arm, train, and support the ___E:SDF U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Democratic_Forces)___ fighting ISIL with airstrikes continued in 2017  through the years 2018–2021 and into the present.

In Il Giornale , ___E:Fausto Biloslavo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fausto_Biloslavo)___ wrote that, despite the program's secrecy, US Vice President ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ was photographed at the center of ___E:Zarqa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zarqa)___ in March 2015.

In April 2014, ___E:Seymour Hersh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seymour_Hersh)___ wrote an essay published in the London Review of Books which does not mention Timber Sycamore but which describes an anonymous former senior US intelligence official's claims that the U.S. diplomatic post in Libya's ___E:Benghazi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benghazi)___ "had no real political role" and existed solely to provide cover for a secret arms pipeline supporting Syrian rebels fighting in the Syrian Civil War in early 2012.  According to Hersh's source, the "rat line" was a means for channeling military weapons from ___E:Gaddafi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaddafi)___ 's arsenals into Syria and into the hands of Syrian rebels.

According to Hersh, an agreement in early 2012 between Obama and Erdoğan proposed an operation funded by Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and conducted by the CIA in collaboration with ___E:MI6 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MI6)___ , although a spokesperson for then CIA director ___E:David Petraeus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Petraeus)___ said the operation never happened.

In 2016, US Senator ___E:Ron Wyden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Wyden)___ 's office questioned the program, releasing a statement that "the US is trying to build up the battlefield capabilities of the anti-Assad opposition, but they haven't provided the public with details about how this is being done, which US agencies are involved, or which foreign partners those agencies are working with."

___E:Thomas Joscelyn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Joscelyn)___ of The Weekly Standard supported the Trump administration's decision to cancel the program, stating "there is no evidence that any truly moderate force is effectively fighting Assad."  In December 2017, ___E:Max Abrahms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Abrahms)___ of the ___E:Council on Foreign Relations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_on_Foreign_Relations)___ and ___E:John Glaser U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Glaser&action=edit&redlink=1)___ of the ___E:Cato Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cato_Institute)___ observed in the Los Angeles Times that "[ISIL] imploded right after external support for the 'moderate' rebels dried up," which is consistent with studies demonstrating that "external support for the opposition tends to exacerbate and extend civil wars, which usually peter out not through power-sharing agreements among fighting equals, but when one side—typically, the incumbent—achieves dominance."  Political scientist ___E:Federico Manfredi Firmian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Manfredi_Firmian&action=edit&redlink=1)___ called Timber Sycamore “one of the United States’ most ill-conceived and deadly covert-action programs,” noting that it failed to unseat Assad, fueled the war, and inflicted untold misery on the Syrian people.  ___E:Jeffrey Sachs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Sachs)___ and ___E:Bob Dreyfuss U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dreyfuss)___ said that the ___E:Obama administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_administration)___ 's aim in the Timber Sycamore program was to overthrow the government of Bashar al-Assad.

Charles Lister, a senior fellow at the ___E:Middle East Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East_Institute)___ , criticized the Obama administration for not providing adequate funding and "necessary resources" to FSA units.

He said that this indecision resulted in the program's failure to decisively shift the strategic dynamics of the war in favor of the ___E:Free Syrian Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Syrian_Army)___ .

According to Lister, the Timber Sycamore program was "drip-feeding ___E:opposition groups U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_opposition)___ just enough to survive but never enough to become dominant actors".

In 2016, Canadian right-wing political commentator ___E:Rachel Marsden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Marsden)___ , in a column in The Baltimore Sun , provided her interpretation of the New York Times reporting on Timber Sycamore.

She suggested that the Timber Sycamore program involved the arming and funding of independent military contractors by the ___E:Saudi intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Intelligence)___ , along with the ___E:CIA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ 's training of pro-American militias in Syria, and that these operations aimed at overthrowing the ___E:Assad government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assad_government)___ , installing a new Syrian government friendly to U.S., Saudi and ___E:Qatari U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar)___ interests, and weaken Russia's influence in the Middle East.  In 2016, Australian columnist ___E:Paul Malone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paul_Malone&action=edit&redlink=1)___ wrote in the Sydney Morning Herald that weapons delivered to various ___E:Free Syrian militias U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Syrian_militias)___ might have been captured by the ___E:Al-Nusra Front U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Nusra_Front)___ , outlining a parallel with the seizure of American weaponry by the Islamic State organization after its ___E:capture of Mosul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mosul_(2014))___ in 2014.
